Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces, and let $r$ be the number of positive singular values of $T$.
Then there exist orthonormal bases $(e_1,\dots,e_n)$ of $V$ and
$(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ of $W$, together with singular values

$$s_1\ge\cdots\ge s_r>0,$$

such that

$$Tv=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j\langle v,e_j\rangle f_j$$

for every $v\in V$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

derivations.claim: Put $A=V-W$, and let $(r_j)$ be an orthonormal basis of $R$. By [F1], diagonalizing $A^*A$ in a right singular basis shows that $(A\otimes I_R)^*(A\otimes I_R)=A^*A\otimes I_R$ has the same largest eigenvalue as $A^*A$: its eigenvectors are the products of right singular vectors of $A$ with the $r_j$, and its eigenvalues are the corresponding squared singular values. Therefore $\|V_R-W_R\|_{\rm op}=\|A\otimes I_R\|_{\rm op}=\|A\|_{\rm op}\le\delta$. For every unit vector $\psi\in H\otimes R$, the vectors $a=V_R\psi$ and $b=W_R\psi$ have norm one and satisfy $\|a-b\|\le\delta$.

For $Z=V_R\rho V_R^*$, positivity follows from $y^*Zy=(V_R^*y)^*\rho(V_R^*y)\ge0$ for every $y$; the same holds with $W_R$. For a vector $z\in K\otimes R$, the entry-sum formula gives $z^*(\operatorname{Tr}_E\otimes I_R)Zz=\sum_e (I_K\otimes|e\rangle\otimes I_R\,z)^*Z(I_K\otimes|e\rangle\otimes I_R\,z)\ge0$, and likewise for $W_R$; hence both reduced outputs are positive. That formula also gives $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_E\otimes I_R)Z)=\operatorname{tr}Z$. Since $V_R^*V_R=W_R^*W_R=I$, cyclicity of finite matrix trace gives $\operatorname{tr}Z=\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ for both outputs. Thus $\rho_V,\rho_W$ are density matrices.

In an orthonormal basis of $\operatorname{span}\{a,b\}$, write $b=za+s e_2$, where $z=a^*b$, $s=\sqrt{1-|z|^2}$, and $e_2\perp a$ is unit if $s>0$. The matrix of $aa^*-bb^*$ on this span is Hermitian, has trace zero and determinant $-s^2$, so its eigenvalues are $s,-s$; outside the span it is zero. Thus $\tfrac12\|aa^*-bb^*\|_1=s$. Also $s^2=1-|z|^2\le2-2\operatorname{Re}z=\|a-b\|^2$, because the difference of the right side and left side is $|1-z|^2$. This proves $D(aa^*,bb^*)\le\delta$ for every pure input, including $s=0$.

Let $X$ be Hermitian on $K\otimes E\otimes R$, and set $Y=(\operatorname{Tr}_E\otimes I_R)X$. For a matrix $B$ on $K\otimes R$, define $\widetilde B$ on $K\otimes E\otimes R$ by applying $B$ to the $K,R$ coordinates and leaving the $E$ coordinate fixed. The entry-sum definition of partial trace gives $\operatorname{tr}(B^*Y)=\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde B^*X)$. Reordering the product basis from $K,E,R$ to $K,R,E$ conjugates $\widetilde B$ to $B\otimes I_E$, so $\|\widetilde B\|_{\rm op}=\|B\|_{\rm op}$ by the same singular-basis argument as in step 1.1. For any square matrix $X=U\Sigma V^*$, [F1] gives its singular value decomposition, and $|\operatorname{tr}(C^*X)|=|\operatorname{tr}(V^*C^*U\Sigma)|\le\|C\|_{\rm op}\sum_j\Sigma_{jj}=\|C\|_{\rm op}\|X\|_1,$ since every diagonal entry of a contraction has modulus at most one. Taking the supremum over $\|B\|_{\rm op}\le1$, and using the equality case $B=U_YV_Y^*$ in a singular value decomposition of $Y$, proves $\|Y\|_1\le\|X\|_1$. This dual formula also gives the triangle inequality and homogeneity for $\|\cdot\|_1$ by applying it to a sum and scalar multiple.

For a pure input $\rho=\psi\psi^*$, step 2.1 bounds the trace distance before discarding $E$, and step 2.2 shows the partial trace cannot increase the trace norm of the Hermitian difference. Hence the reduced output distance is at most $\delta$. For general positive trace-one $\rho$, [F2] gives a spectral decomposition $\rho=\sum_j p_j\psi_j\psi_j^*$ with $p_j\ge0$ and $\sum_jp_j=1$. The maps and partial trace are linear; the triangle inequality and homogeneity from step 2.2 therefore bound the reduced output distance by $\sum_jp_j\delta=\delta$.

In this page a **Hamiltonian** is a self-adjoint endomorphism $H$ of a
finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $V$; no physical postulate is
part of the term. Let $\sigma(H)$ be the set of its distinct eigenvalues and
let $P_\lambda$ be the orthogonal projection onto the $\lambda$-eigenspace.
For real time $t$, define the finite matrix evolution

$$U_H(t):=\sum_{\lambda\in\sigma(H)}e^{-it\lambda}P_\lambda = f_t(H),\qquad f_t(\lambda)=e^{-it\lambda}.$$

The second expression uses the finite spectral functional calculus
[[def-functional-calculus-for-a-normal-endomorphism]]. If $V$ is the zero
space, the spectrum is empty and the empty sum is the unique endomorphism,
which is also the identity on $V$. This definition specifies a mathematical
unitary from a finite matrix; it makes no claim that the operation has an
efficient circuit or a free access cost.

For all $z,w\in\mathbb C$, $\exp(z+w)=\exp z\exp w$. For real $x$, the complex value $\exp(x+0i)$ equals the published real exponential $e^x$. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[def-complex-exponential]], [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]], [[lem-cauchy-product-of-absolutely-convergent-complex-series]], [[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]], [[lem-binomial-theorem-over-complex-numbers]], [[thm-binomial-closed-formula]].

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

For real $x,y$, $\exp(x+iy)=e^x(\cos y+i\sin y)$ and $|\exp(x+iy)|=e^x$. In particular $e^{i\pi}+1=0$. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]], [[thm-eulers-formula]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]], [[thm-pythagorean-and-parity-identities-for-all-six-trigonometric-functions]], [[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]], [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]], [[def-pi-via-first-positive-cosine-zero]].

derivations.claim: The map $V_x$ permutes the finite orthonormal basis and satisfies $V_x^2=I$, so it is unitary. In a term indexed by $i,b$, the endpoints become $|i-1,b\oplus p_{i-1}\rangle$ and $|i,b\oplus x_i\oplus p_i\rangle$. Since $p_i=p_{i-1}\oplus x_i$, the second bit is $b\oplus p_{i-1}$; the edge is therefore an ordinary adjacent path edge with the spectator bit unchanged. Thus $V_xH_xV_x$ is two identical path matrices $H_0$, one for each bit $b$, and $V_x$ fixes $|0,0\rangle$ while sending $|n,0\rangle$ to $|n,p_n\rangle$.

Let $|D_i^n\rangle$ be the normalized uniform superposition of $n$-bit strings of Hamming weight $i$, and set $|D_{-1}^n\rangle=|D_{n+1}^n\rangle=0$. Counting the $i$ downward flips and $n-i$ upward flips gives $J|D_i^n\rangle=\tfrac12\sqrt{i(n+1-i)}|D_{i-1}^n\rangle+\tfrac12\sqrt{(i+1)(n-i)}|D_{i+1}^n\rangle$ for every $0\le i\le n$. Thus $(2/n)J$ has the stated path weights on the symmetric subspace.

Each Pauli $X_r$ has eigenvalues $\pm1$, so [F2] gives $\|X_r\|_{\rm op}=1$. The triangle inequality then gives $\|J\|_{\rm op}\le n/2$, so $\|H_0\|_{\rm op}\le1$; unitary conjugation in step 1.1 gives $\|H_x\|_{\rm op}\le1$.

For each sign string $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^n$, put $u_\sigma=2^{-n/2}\sum_{y\in\{0,1\}^n}(\prod_r\sigma_r^{y_r})|y\rangle$. Factorizing the finite inner-product sum gives $\langle u_\sigma,u_\tau\rangle=2^{-n}\prod_r(1+\sigma_r\tau_r)$, so these $2^n$ vectors form an orthonormal basis. Flipping bit $r$ gives $X_ru_\sigma=\sigma_ru_\sigma$. By [F1]–[F2], $e^{-i(\pi/2)\sum_rX_r}$ acts on $u_\sigma$ by $\exp(-i\pi\sum_r\sigma_r/2)$. The scalar addition law in [F1] factors this as $\prod_r\exp(-i\pi\sigma_r/2)$, and Euler's formula [F3] gives each factor as $-i\sigma_r$. Hence $e^{-i(\pi/2)\sum_rX_r}=(-i)^nX_1\cdots X_n$. This maps $|D_0^n\rangle=|0^n\rangle$ to $(-i)^n|D_n^n\rangle=(-i)^n|1^n\rangle$. The path basis identifies $|D_0^n\rangle,|D_n^n\rangle$ with $|0\rangle,|n\rangle$; step 1.1 then sends the endpoint to $|n,p_n\rangle$. The time $t=\pi n/2$ for $H_0=(2/n)J$ is time $\pi/2$ for $J$, proving the transfer identity.

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let $K=K^*$ on $H$, and let $\alpha>0$ satisfy $\|K\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\alpha$. Put $A=K/\alpha$. Let $U$ be a unitary on an ancilla-system space $H_A\otimes H$, let $J:H\to H_A\otimes H$ be the isometry $Jv=|0^a\rangle\otimes v$, and let $\Pi=JJ^*$. An **exact Hermitian block encoding** is the data $(U,J,\alpha)$ with $J^*UJ=A$. The matrix $K$ is Hermitian; $U$ itself need not be Hermitian.

The signal-register reflection is $R_\Pi=2\Pi-I$. The access record lists, separately, each supplied call to $U$, $U^*$, controlled-$U$, controlled-$U^*$, and $R_\Pi$, together with their circuit, query, gate, width, ancilla, precision, and classical-generation costs from [[def-qa-22-block-encoding-access-model]] and [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]. A state description or block matrix alone supplies none of these calls. A controlled reflection is also separate. Any PREPARE, SELECT, sparse-location, value, or coefficient operation used by a construction is a separately supplied, reversible interface with its inverse and cost recorded.

Here is the standard-form **qubiterate** for this access instance. Add a flag qubit and define $\widetilde U=|0\rangle\langle0|\otimes U+|1\rangle\langle1|\otimes U^*$, $J'v=|+\rangle\otimes Jv$, $S=X\otimes I$, $F=S\widetilde U$, and $W_{\mathrm q}=(2J'J'^*-I)F$. Implementing $\widetilde U$ requires the separately declared controlled-$U$ and controlled-$U^*$ calls; $S$, the preparation of $|+\rangle$, and the reflection about $\operatorname{ran}(J')$ also have declared costs. [[thm-qa-25-qubitization-signal-sequence]] proves its compressed block and spectral relation.

For the QSVT simulation sequence, the signal operations are the alternating $U,U^*$ calls interleaved with the projector phases $e^{i\phi(2\Pi-I)}$ from [[def-qa-23-qsp-signal-sequence]]. Their exact phase list, parity, real-polynomial extraction, controls, inverse calls, and phase-synthesis precision are part of the supplied circuit description. The scalar polynomial pairs must satisfy [[def-qa-23-qsp-admissible-polynomial-pair]]; singular-value transformations use the convention of [[def-qa-24-singular-value-transform]].

Let $A:H_R\to H_L$ be the PUE map of [[def-qa-24-pue-svd-data]], with positive singular pairs $(\sigma_j,v_j,u_j)$. For every $0<\sigma_j<1$, set

$$w_j=\frac{(I-\Pi_R)U^*u_j}{\sqrt{1-\sigma_j^2}},\qquad \widetilde w_j=\frac{(I-\Pi_L)Uv_j}{\sqrt{1-\sigma_j^2}}.$$

The vectors $w_j$ form an orthonormal family in $\ker\Pi_R$ and the vectors $\widetilde w_j$ form an orthonormal family in $\ker\Pi_L$. In the input basis $(v_j,w_j)$ and output basis $(u_j,\widetilde w_j)$,

$$U\big|_{\operatorname{span}(v_j,w_j)}=\begin{pmatrix}\sigma_j&\sqrt{1-\sigma_j^2}\\\sqrt{1-\sigma_j^2}&-\sigma_j\end{pmatrix}.$$

For $\sigma_j=1$, $Uv_j=u_j$ and the complementary vector is absent. A right zero-singular vector $v\in\ker A\cap H_R$ satisfies $Uv\in\ker\Pi_L$; a left zero-singular vector $u\in\ker A^*\cap H_L$ satisfies $U^*u\in\ker\Pi_R$. Let $M_R$ be the orthogonal sum of all positive-singular input planes or lines, $\ker A$, and $U^*(\ker A^*)$; let $M_L$ be the corresponding sum of positive-singular output planes or lines, $U(\ker A)$, and $\ker A^*$. Then $U(M_R)=M_L$. The residual ambient subspaces $M_R^\perp$ and $M_L^\perp$ lie in $\ker\Pi_R$ and $\ker\Pi_L$, and $U(M_R^\perp)=M_L^\perp$. Thus each named block is invariant under its corresponding projector, with no implicit pairing of the two kernels.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

Let $V,W$ be inner product spaces ([[def-inner-product-space]]) over the same field and let $T:V\to W$ be linear ([[def-linear-map]]). An **adjoint** of $T$ is a linear map $T^*:W\to V$ such that

$$\langle Tv,w\rangle_W=\langle v,T^*w\rangle_V$$

for every $v\in V$ and $w\in W$. Existence is not part of the definition; in finite dimensions it will follow from Riesz representation.

Write $T^{\dagger}$ for the adjoint $T^*$ characterized by [[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]]. Fix integers $m,n\ge1$, $a\ge0$, and $d\ge\max(m,n)$. On each coordinate space $\mathbb C^r$ use $\langle x,y\rangle_{\rm root}:=\sum_{q=1}^r x_q\overline{y_q}$, linear in the first argument. Put the ancilla register before the system register in every tensor product, and let $e_0=(1,0,\ldots,0)$ be the first standard basis vector in $\mathbb C^{2^a}$. For $A:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^m$, choose as part of the data padding maps $E_{\rm in}:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^d$ and $E_{\rm out}:\mathbb C^m\to\mathbb C^d$ satisfying $E_{\rm in}^{\dagger}E_{\rm in}=I_n$ and $E_{\rm out}^{\dagger}E_{\rm out}=I_m$. The default padding sends a coordinate vector to the same coordinates followed by zeros. Set $\widehat A:=E_{\rm out}AE_{\rm in}^{\dagger}:\mathbb C^d\to\mathbb C^d$.

Let $J_a:\mathbb C^d\to\mathbb C^{2^a}\otimes\mathbb C^d$ be $J_ax=e_0\otimes x$, where $e_0$ is the all-zero computational basis vector, and let $\Pi_a:=J_aJ_a^{\dagger}$. For a unitary $U$ on $\mathbb C^{2^a}\otimes\mathbb C^d$, its **projected block** is the endomorphism $B_U:=J_a^{\dagger}UJ_a$ of $\mathbb C^d$. It is not asserted to be unitary.

For $\alpha>0$ and $\varepsilon\ge0$, the tuple $(U,a,\alpha,\varepsilon,d,E_{\rm in},E_{\rm out})$ is an **$(\alpha,a,\varepsilon)$ block encoding of $A$** when $\alpha\ge\|A\|_{\rm op}$ and $\|B_U-\widehat A/\alpha\|_{\rm op}\le\varepsilon$. The exact case is $\varepsilon=0$. For square $A$, take $m=n=d$ and both embeddings equal to the identity. For rectangular $A$, the dimensions and embeddings remain part of the encoding data.

The equivalent projector notation identifies $B_U$ with the restriction of $\Pi_aU\Pi_a$ to $\operatorname{ran}(\Pi_a)$, transported to $\mathbb C^d$ by $J_a$; it does not regard $\Pi_aU\Pi_a$ as a unitary.

derivations.claim: Fix an eigenvector $\psi_j$ with unit norm and write $v_j=J\psi_j$. From [F1], $\Pi Uv_j=x_jv_j$ and $\Pi U^*v_j=x_jv_j$, because $K=K^*$. Since $U,U^*$ preserve norm, orthogonal decomposition by $\Pi$ gives $\|(I-\Pi)Uv_j\|^2=\|(I-\Pi)U^*v_j\|^2=1-x_j^2=s_j^2$. For $|x_j|<1$, the displayed $\eta_j,\widetilde\eta_j$ are therefore unit vectors in $\ker\Pi$.

If $i\ne j$, orthogonality of eigenvectors and [F4] give $\langle Uv_i,Uv_j\rangle=\langle v_i,v_j\rangle=0$, while $\langle\Pi Uv_i,\Pi Uv_j\rangle=x_ix_j\langle v_i,v_j\rangle=0$. Subtracting the projected components shows $\langle\eta_i,\eta_j\rangle=0$; the same calculation for $U^*$ proves orthogonality of the $\widetilde\eta_j$.

Decomposing $Uv_j$ into its $\Pi$ and $I-\Pi$ parts gives $Uv_j=x_jv_j+s_j\eta_j$. Also $s_jU\widetilde\eta_j=U(I-\Pi)U^*v_j=v_j-U\Pi U^*v_j=v_j-x_jUv_j=s_j^2v_j-x_js_j\eta_j.$ Division by $s_j>0$ yields $U\widetilde\eta_j=s_jv_j-x_j\eta_j$, which is the second column of the displayed matrix. Taking adjoints gives the reverse-basis action of $U^*$.

If $|x_j|=1$, the orthogonal complement of $\Pi Uv_j=x_jv_j$ has squared norm $1-|x_j|^2=0$, so $Uv_j=x_jv_j$; the same argument for $U^*$ gives $U^*v_j=x_jv_j$. Thus the endpoint plane collapses. At $x_j=0$, step 1.1 has $s_j=1$, so both normalized vectors are well-defined. The mutually orthogonal paired spaces and endpoint lines exhaust the clean input and output signal spaces by the SVD decomposition in [F2]; their orthogonal residual complements stay in $\ker\Pi$ and cannot contribute to the clean compression.

$$\eta_j=(I-\Pi)UJ\psi_j/s_j,\qquad \widetilde\eta_j=(I-\Pi)U^*J\psi_j/s_j.$$
The $\eta_j$ are orthonormal in $\ker\Pi$, as are the $\widetilde\eta_j$. In the paired input basis $(J\psi_j,\widetilde\eta_j)$ and output basis $(J\psi_j,\eta_j)$, $U$ has matrix
$$\begin{pmatrix}x_j&s_j\\s_j&-x_j\end{pmatrix}.$$
The unitary $U^*$ maps in the reverse direction by the same matrix. If $|x_j|=1$, the complement is absent and $UJ\psi_j=x_jJ\psi_j=U^*J\psi_j$; no division by zero is used. The value $x_j=0$ is an ordinary two-dimensional signal plane.

Let $x\in[-1,1]$, put $s(x)=\sqrt{1-x^2}$ using the nonnegative real square root, and define the Hermitian-reflection signal matrix
$$W_R(x)=\begin{pmatrix}x&s(x)\\s(x)&-x\end{pmatrix}.$$
For each real $\phi$, define $Z(\phi)=\operatorname{diag}(e^{i\phi},e^{-i\phi})$. For an integer $d\ge0$ and real phase list $\Phi=(\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_d)$, the length-$d$ QSP sequence is the ordered matrix product
$$U_\Phi(x)=Z(\phi_0)\prod_{j=1}^{d}\bigl(W_R(x)Z(\phi_j)\bigr),$$
where the product is written left to right in increasing $j$ and matrix multiplication acts right to left. For $d=0$ this is $Z(\phi_0)$. This definition fixes the sign of the off-diagonal signal entry, both endpoint phases, and the product order.

The phases are in matrix order: when the factors are applied as chronological circuit layers, the rightmost factor acts first, in accordance with [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]]. In the ordered signal basis, if both coordinates are nonzero, applying $Z(\phi)$ multiplies the ratio of the second coordinate to the first by $e^{-2i\phi}$; if either coordinate is zero, that relative phase is undefined, while the displayed matrix action remains defined. This is the relative phase convention fixed by [[def-qc-relative-phase]].

Let $A:H_R\to H_L$ be the PUE map of [[def-qa-24-pue-svd-data]], with positive singular pairs $(\sigma_j,v_j,u_j)$, and let $\Phi=(\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_d)$ be the exact phase list in [[alg-qa-24-qsvt]]. Let $P_\Phi$ be the upper-left scalar polynomial of its QSP signal sequence. On every positive two-dimensional singular plane from [[lem-qa-24-pue-svd-invariant-subspaces]], the QSVT sequence is exactly $U_\Phi(\sigma_j)$. Consequently, if $d$ is odd,

$$\Pi_LU_\Phi\Pi_R\big|_{H_R}=\sum_{j=1}^{r}P_\Phi(\sigma_j)|u_j\rangle\langle v_j|=\bigl(P_\Phi\bigr)^{\mathrm{SV}}_{\mathrm{odd}}(A),$$

and if $d$ is even,

$$\Pi_RU_\Phi\Pi_R\big|_{H_R}=\sum_{j=1}^{r}P_\Phi(\sigma_j)|v_j\rangle\langle v_j|+P_\Phi(0)\Pi_{\ker A}=\bigl(P_\Phi\bigr)^{\mathrm{SV}}_R(A).$$

The formulas include singular values $0$ and $1$, repeated singular values, unmatched left and right kernels, and zero-dimensional singular spaces. If $p\in\mathbb R[x]$ has parity $d\bmod2$ and $|p(x)|\le1$ on $[-1,1]$, the exact completion and phase-factorization suppliers give a phase list with $\operatorname{Re}P_\Phi=p$. A **promise problem** is a pair $(Y,N)$ of disjoint subsets of $\{0,1\}^*$. Its promise is $Y\cup N$. A deterministic solver must accept every word of $Y$ and reject every word of $N$, with either answer allowed elsewhere. The pair belongs to $\mathrm{PromiseP}$ if such a solver has a polynomial time bound on every input.

It belongs to $\mathrm{PromiseNP}$ if there are a polynomial $p$ and a deterministic polynomial-time predicate $V(x,w)$ such that every $x\in Y$ has some $w$ with $|w|\le p(|x|)$ and $V(x,w)=1$, whereas for every $x\in N$ every such $w$ has $V(x,w)=0$. The promise need not be decidable; either side or both sides may be empty. When $Y\cup N=\{0,1\}^*$, this is the ordinary language decision convention.

A **full-list uniform quantum circuit family** is a sequence $(C_n)_{n\ge0}$ together with one fixed deterministic one-tape Turing machine $G$ and constants $c\ge1$ and $k\in\mathbb N$ such that, on input the unary word $1^n$, $G$ halts within $c(n+1)^k$ transitions and its final tape is a valid self-delimiting binary description of the entire circuit $C_n$. A self-delimiting binary natural $r$ is written $1^{|\operatorname{bin}(r)|}0\operatorname{bin}(r)$, where $\operatorname{bin}(r)$ is its ordinary binary numeral with no leading zeros and $\operatorname{bin}(0)=0$. Each gate record consists of a two-bit label ($00,01,10,11$ for $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$ respectively), followed by one self-delimiting wire index for $H,T,T^\dagger$ and two ordered self-delimiting indices for CNOT. Every index is less than $m$; CNOT indices are distinct, with the first the control and the second the target. The list contains exactly $g$ records. After the gate list, an output-count self-delimiting natural is followed by that many ordered, pairwise distinct wire indices, each less than $m$. Parsing rejects every other label, malformed or out-of-range index, repeated output index, truncated field, or trailing bit. This defines a total decoder by returning a fixed malformed-code symbol on any invalid word; effective binary encodings and total decoders are as in [[def-effective-binary-encoding-and-decoder]].

on the ordered input and target computational basis, where XOR is componentwise. derivations.claim: The maximum weight satisfies $1/2\le \max_iw_i\le1$: $i(n+1-i)\le(n+1)^2/4\le n^2$ gives the upper bound, and a central integer $i$ has $i(n+1-i)\ge n^2/4$ for the lower bound. Every edge satisfies $i(n+1-i)-n=(i-1)(n-i)\ge0$, so $w_i\ge w_1=1/\sqrt n>\eta$. The grid spacing $2^{-b}\le1/(3\pi n)=2\eta$, hence nearest rounding gives $|q_i-w_i|\le\eta$ and $q_i>0$; the support is unchanged. It follows that each row and column of $E_x=\widetilde H_x-H_x$ has at most two nonzero entries, each of magnitude at most $\eta$, and $2/9<\max_iq_i<2$; in particular $2\max_iq_i$ is bounded above and below by positive constants independent of $n,x$.

Order path vertices lexicographically by $(i,b_0)$. A location query's predecessor slot, when present, uses only $x_i$, and its successor slot, when present, uses only $x_{i+1}$; their order is fixed by the path index. For an arbitrary candidate pair of vertices, the value query tests the single relevant edge bit and returns the known dyadic $q_i$ or zero. Each oracle function can thus be computed reversibly using one parity-bit query into scratch, an XOR into the requested target, and a second parity-bit query to erase scratch. The same construction controls the target XOR by any query-control bit, so each controlled or uncontrolled sparse-oracle call costs at most two calls to the parity-bit oracle. The x-independent $q_i$ table is generated by integer arithmetic: binary search finds the nearest grid point by comparing squared integers with $2^{2b}i(n+1-i)/n^2$, using $O(\log(n+1))$-bit numbers and polynomially many steps in $n$. On $x\in[-1,1]$ the scalar target is $f_\tau(x)=\exp(-i\tau x)$; if $H\psi_\lambda=\lambda\psi_\lambda$, then $f_\tau(\lambda/\alpha)=\exp(-it\lambda)$, the eigenvalue of the finite matrix evolution [[def-qa-19-finite-matrix-dynamics]].

For $k\ge0$, define the Chebyshev polynomials by $T_0(x)=1$, $T_1(x)=x$, $T_{k+1}(x)=2xT_k(x)-T_{k-1}(x)$. Define the Bessel coefficients used here by the series
$$J_k(\tau)=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^j(\tau/2)^{2j+k}}{j!(j+k)!}.$$
For fixed $k,\tau$, the ratio of consecutive absolute summands is $\tau^2/[4(j+1)(j+k+1)]\to0$, so this series converges absolutely and defines $J_k(\tau)$ before any estimate is used. The exponential uses the series convention of [[def-complex-exponential]], whose absolute convergence is supplied by [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]]. This definition specifies the target and coefficient series; it does not assert a Jacobi–Anger expansion or a truncation bound. A real QSP or QSVT theorem alone does not implement this full complex, non-parity target; the finite even/odd combination, complementary-polynomial certificates, normalization, and controlled relative phase are separate operations in the binding simulator.

Let $\iota_{\mathbb R}\colon\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$ be the canonical-natural map
of [[def-canonical-natural]], and let $j\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ be the real
embedding $j(x)=x+i0$ from [[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]. For every
$n\in\mathbb N$, the factorial $n!$ is nonzero by
[[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]], so
$\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!)>0$ by [[lem-of-naturals-positive]] and consequently
$j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))\ne0$ in the complex field
[[thm-complex-numbers-form-a-field]].

For $z\in\mathbb C$, define
$$ \exp z:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^n}{j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))}. $$
whenever this complex series converges. Inside a complex expression we
abbreviate the embedded denominator $j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))$ by $n!$, so the
same definition may be written $\exp z=\sum z^n/n!$ without identifying a
natural number with a complex number. Powers and series are those of
[[def-complex-integer-powers]] and
[[def-complex-series-power-series-and-absolute-convergence]]. The convergence
for every $z\in\mathbb C$ is discharged by
[[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]].
For every $z\in\mathbb C$, the series $\sum z^n/n!$ converges absolutely.

For real $x,y$, $\exp(x+iy)=e^x(\cos y+i\sin y)$ and $|\exp(x+iy)|=e^x$. In particular $e^{i\pi}+1=0$. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]], [[thm-eulers-formula]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]], [[thm-pythagorean-and-parity-identities-for-all-six-trigonometric-functions]], [[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]], [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]], [[def-pi-via-first-positive-cosine-zero]].

The input description also supplies terminating certified comparisons and rational-interval evaluations for the scalar arithmetic below. A bounded block-error input is a separate variant with a certified block-error budget; it is not silently treated as exact.

**Output.** Return the finite circuit list and error certificate for a unitary dilation $V_{\rm impl}$. Its success claim is on the clean-input isometry $J_{\rm clean}|\psi\rangle=|0_{\rm work}\rangle|\psi\rangle$; auxiliary output registers are approximate and are not measured to clean an unknown system input. On a failed polynomial or phase certificate, return the phase routine's declared failure status and do not report a simulator.

**Generation and execution.** Set $\tau=\alpha t$ and $\rho=\epsilon^2/10000$. For $t=0$, return the identity circuit and zero query count. Otherwise:

1. Starting at $d=\max(1,\lceil|\tau|\rceil)$, increase $d$ until $u=|\tau|/(2(d+2))<1$ and
   $$\frac{2(|\tau|/2)^{d+1}}{(d+1)!(1-u)}\le\rho/8.$$
   Evaluate each strict comparison by the certified interval routine named in OP0 of the binding operational appendix; an undecided equality is not rounded toward success.
2. For each $k=0,\ldots,d$, compute $J_k(\tau)$ from the series in [[def-qa-25-hamiltonian-simulation-polynomial]]. Stop its alternating-series evaluation only after its ratio $\tau^2/[4(j+1)(j+k+1)]$ is below $1$ and its geometric remainder is at most $\rho/(32(d+1))$. Store a rational coefficient and its error interval. Form $T_0=1,T_1=x,T_{k+1}=2xT_k-T_{k-1}$. Set
   $$E=J_0+2\sum_{1\le 2r\le d}(-1)^rJ_{2r}T_{2r},\qquad O=2\sum_{1\le 2r+1\le d}(-1)^rJ_{2r+1}T_{2r+1}.$$
   Thus $Q:=E-iO$ is the rounded Jacobi–Anger truncation and its certified scalar error is $\|Q-f_\tau\|_{[-1,1]}\le\rho$; the sign $(-i)^k$ is literal.
3. Require a certified combined polynomial error at most $\rho$. Then $|E(x)|,|O(x)|\le1+\rho$ on $[-1,1]$. Put $B=1+2\rho$, $p_E=E/B$, and $p_O=O/B$. Execute each real QSVT extraction using [[alg-qa-24-qsvt]] and the exact signal access of [[def-qa-25-qubitization-access-model]]. If an extraction fails certification, return that failure.

SELECT applies the $p_E(H/\alpha)$ block in branch $0$ and $-i$ times the $p_O(H/\alpha)$ block in branch $1$. Unprepare the coefficient qubit. The resulting clean block before amplification is $M/2$, where $M=p_E(H/\alpha)-i p_O(H/\alpha)=Q(H/\alpha)/B$. Since $B=1+2\rho$, the scalar error bound gives
$$\|M-e^{-itH}\|_{\rm op}\le\frac{\rho}{B}+\frac{B-1}{B}=\frac{3\rho}{1+2\rho}<3\rho;$$
here $f_\tau(H/\alpha)=e^{-itH}$ by finite spectral calculus and $|f_\tau(x)|=1$. The factor $-i$ is a relative phase under any outer control and is not discarded.
5. Apply the explicit phase-corrected oblivious-amplitude-amplification unitary $C=-WRW^*RW$, where $R=I-2\Pi_{\rm zero}$ and $W$ is the complete even/odd block-combination circuit. Retain its work registers. Allocate total phase, gate, and block implementation error at most $\epsilon/4$ after amplification. Put $L=\ln(1/\epsilon)>0$, $\tau_0=|\tau|>\epsilon$, and $S=\tau_0+L/\ln(e+L/\tau_0)$. If $\tau_0\ge1/4$, then $S\ge1/4$. If $\tau_0<1/4$, put $u=1/\tau_0>4$, so $L>\ln u$. The function $g(y)=y/\ln(e+uy)$ is increasing for $y>0$, since its derivative has numerator $\ln(e+uy)-uy/(e+uy)>0$; the first term exceeds $1$ and the second is below $1$. Also $\ln u\le u/2$ for $u\ge4$ (the difference has positive derivative and is positive at $4$), and $e\le u^2/2$, so $e+u\ln u\le u^2$. Therefore $S\ge g(L)>g(\ln u)\ge1/2$. In all cases $S\ge1/4$. Set $m=\lceil64S\rceil$; then $m\ge16$, $m\ge64\tau_0$, and $d=m-1\ge\max(1,\lceil\tau_0\rceil)$, so this is an eligible candidate in the OP4 loop starting rule [F7]. The real parameter $\tau$ is defined in [F1].

For $x=\cos\theta$, [F6] writes $e^{-i\tau x}$ as the product of the absolutely convergent exponential series for $e^{-i\tau e^{i\theta}/2}$ and $e^{-i\tau e^{-i\theta}/2}$. Absolute convergence permits grouping terms by the exponent difference $k$; for each $k\ge0$ the coefficient of $e^{ik\theta}$ is $(-i)^kJ_k(\tau)$, and the coefficient of $e^{-ik\theta}$ is the same. Pairing these terms and using [F1] gives $e^{-i\tau x}=J_0(\tau)+2\sum_{k\ge1}(-i)^kJ_k(\tau)T_k(x).$ By [F1], [F3], [F4], and [F6], the defining product is absolutely and uniformly convergent in $\theta$ on bounded intervals, so the regrouping is valid.

Subtracting the degree-$d$ partial sum in step 2.1, applying the triangle inequality, and using $|T_k(x)|\le1$ from step 1.1 gives error at most $2\sum_{k>d}|J_k(\tau)|$. With $m=d+1$, the ratio of consecutive factorial majorants $(|\tau|/2)^k/k!$ for $k\ge m$ is at most $u=|\tau|/(2(m+1))<1$. The geometric-series bound from step 1.2 now yields the stated factorial tail.

By [F7], each of the $d+1$ OP4 coefficient errors is at most $\rho/(32(d+1))$. Since a nonconstant Chebyshev term has coefficient multiplier $2$, their total uniform contribution is at most $(1+2d)\rho/(32(d+1))<\rho/16$; adding the tail $\rho/8$ from step 3.1 gives a combined error $<\rho$. The coefficients and multiplier $2$ are those of the expansion in [F1].

Let $r=L/\tau_0$. If $r\ge1$, then $m\ge64\tau_0(1+r/\ln(e+r))$. Since $\ln y\le\sqrt y$ for $y\ge1$ and $r/(e+r)\ge1/(e+1)$, we have $r/\ln(e+r)\ge\sqrt{e+r}/(e+1)$. Thus $2m/(e\tau_0)\ge[128/(e(e+1))]\sqrt{e+r}>\sqrt{e+r}$, because $e<3$ gives $128/(e(e+1))>128/12>1$; hence $\ln(2m/(e\tau_0))\ge\frac12\ln(e+r)$. If $r<1$, $m\ge64\tau_0$ gives $2m/(e\tau_0)\ge128/e$, hence $\ln(2m/(e\tau_0))>1$, since $e<3$ implies $128/e>42>e$. For $r\ge1$, these bounds give $m\ln(2m/(e\tau_0))\ge32\tau_0(\ln(e+r)+r)\ge32(L+\tau_0)$, because $\ln(e+r)>1$. For $r<1$, they give $m\ln(2m/(e\tau_0))>64\tau_0>32(L+\tau_0)$, because $L<\tau_0$. Also $u_m=\tau_0/[2(m+1)]\le1/128$, so $2/(1-u_m)\le256/127<4$, and the factorial tail expression is bounded by the estimate of step 3.1. The real $\tau$ is defined in [F1]. $\ln(m!)=\sum_{j=1}^m\ln j\ge\int_1^m\ln x\,dx\ge m\ln m-m,$ so $m!\ge(m/e)^m$. The factorial-tail test at $d=m-1$ is consequently at most $\frac{2(\tau_0/2)^m}{m!(1-u_m)} \le4\exp\!\left(-m\ln\frac{2m}{e\tau_0}\right) \le4e^{-32(L+\tau_0)} \le e^{-2L}/80000=\rho/8.$ The last inequality holds because $L+\tau_0>1$: for $0<\epsilon<1$, the function $\ln(1/\epsilon)-(1-\epsilon)$ is positive (its derivative is $(\epsilon-1)/\epsilon<0$ as $\epsilon$ increases to $1$, and its value at $1$ is zero), and $\tau_0>\epsilon$. Hence $30(L+\tau_0)>30>\ln(320000)$; the numerical comparison follows from $e>2$, which gives $e^{30}>2^{30}>320000$. Since $m\le64S+1\le68S$ using $S\ge1/4$, the passing degree $d=m-1$ is $O(S)$. The factorial tail is the estimate of step 3.1 and the OP4 threshold is [F7].

If $\tau_0\le\epsilon$, the derivative fact [F5] and $|e^{-isx}|=1$ from [F4] give $e^{-i\tau x}-1=\int_0^\tau -ix e^{-isx}\,ds,\qquad |e^{-i\tau x}-1|\le|\tau x|\le\epsilon$ for every $x\in[-1,1]$. Thus the wrapper [F8] has the stated small-time error, including $\tau=0$.

**Inputs.** A finite Hermitian $H$, $\alpha>0$, an exact $(\alpha,a,0)$ block encoding $U$ with $J^*UJ=H/\alpha$, a rational time $t$, rational $0<\epsilon\le1$, and separately declared access and cost for $U,U^*,$ controlled-$U$, controlled-$U^*$, both projector-phase circuits, coefficient preparation, SELECT, OAA reflections, phase synthesis, data access, and classical arithmetic. The input description also supplies terminating certified comparisons and rational-interval evaluations for the scalar arithmetic below. A bounded block-error input is a separate variant with a certified block-error budget; it is not silently treated as exact.

**Output.** Return the finite circuit list and error certificate for a unitary dilation $V_{\rm impl}$. Its success claim is on the clean-input isometry $J_{\rm clean}|\psi\rangle=|0_{\rm work}\rangle|\psi\rangle$; auxiliary output registers are approximate and are not measured to clean an unknown system input. On a failed polynomial or phase certificate, return the phase routine's declared failure status and do not report a simulator.

**Generation and execution.** Set $\tau=\alpha t$ and $\rho=\epsilon^2/10000$. For $t=0$, return the identity circuit and zero query count. Otherwise:

1. Starting at $d=\max(1,\lceil|\tau|\rceil)$, increase $d$ until $u=|\tau|/(2(d+2))<1$ and
   $$\frac{2(|\tau|/2)^{d+1}}{(d+1)!(1-u)}\le\rho/8.$$
   Evaluate each strict comparison by the certified interval routine named in OP0 of the binding operational appendix; an undecided equality is not rounded toward success.
2. For each $k=0,\ldots,d$, compute $J_k(\tau)$ from the series in [[def-qa-25-hamiltonian-simulation-polynomial]]. Stop its alternating-series evaluation only after its ratio $\tau^2/[4(j+1)(j+k+1)]$ is below $1$ and its geometric remainder is at most $\rho/(32(d+1))$. Store a rational coefficient and its error interval. Form $T_0=1,T_1=x,T_{k+1}=2xT_k-T_{k-1}$. Set
   $$E=J_0+2\sum_{1\le 2r\le d}(-1)^rJ_{2r}T_{2r},\qquad O=2\sum_{1\le 2r+1\le d}(-1)^rJ_{2r+1}T_{2r+1}.$$
   Thus $Q:=E-iO$ is the rounded Jacobi–Anger truncation and its certified scalar error is $\|Q-f_\tau\|_{[-1,1]}\le\rho$; the sign $(-i)^k$ is literal.
3. Require a certified combined polynomial error at most $\rho$. Then $|E(x)|,|O(x)|\le1+\rho$ on $[-1,1]$. Put $B=1+2\rho$, $p_E=E/B$, and $p_O=O/B$. Call [[alg-qa-23-qsp-phase-synthesis]] separately on these two real targets with their actual degree and parity, retaining its complementary-polynomial certificate, phase list, precision, and every explicit failure branch. Execute each real QSVT extraction using [[alg-qa-24-qsvt]] and the exact signal access of [[def-qa-25-qubitization-access-model]]. If an extraction fails certification, return that failure.
4. Pad both extraction workspaces to the same ordered register space. Prepare a clean coefficient qubit in $|+\rangle$. SELECT applies the $p_E(H/\alpha)$ block in branch $0$ and $-i$ times the $p_O(H/\alpha)$ block in branch $1$. Unprepare the coefficient qubit. The resulting clean block before amplification is $M/2$, where $M=p_E(H/\alpha)-i p_O(H/\alpha)=Q(H/\alpha)/B$. Since $B=1+2\rho$, the scalar error bound gives
$$\|M-e^{-itH}\|_{\rm op}\le\frac{\rho}{B}+\frac{B-1}{B}=\frac{3\rho}{1+2\rho}<3\rho;$$
here $f_\tau(H/\alpha)=e^{-itH}$ by finite spectral calculus and $|f_\tau(x)|=1$. The factor $-i$ is a relative phase under any outer control and is not discarded.
5. Apply the explicit phase-corrected oblivious-amplitude-amplification unitary $C=-WRW^*RW$, where $R=I-2\Pi_{\rm zero}$ and $W$ is the complete even/odd block-combination circuit. Retain its work registers. Allocate total phase, gate, and block implementation error at most $\epsilon/4$ after amplification. A controlled simulator controls every whole block and the known correction, using the separately supplied controlled access.

The arithmetic, coefficient series, two phase-generation calls, controlled QSVT sequences, coefficient register, SELECT, and OAA list are finite outputs; their gate, query, precision, workspace, description-bit, and classical computation costs are separate coordinates. The phase-generation call is the finite procedure of [[alg-qa-23-qsp-phase-synthesis]], not a free source routine. A sparse input uses its actually supplied block-encoding circuit and its exact row-location, value, precision, and state-preparation costs; standard XOR sparse access alone does not imply an in-place reversible location permutation.

With $J_k,T_k$ defined in [[def-qa-25-hamiltonian-simulation-polynomial]], for every real $\tau$ and integer $d\ge0$,
$$\sup_{|x|\le1}\left|\exp(-i\tau x)-\left(J_0(\tau)+2\sum_{k=1}^{d}(-i)^kJ_k(\tau)T_k(x)\right)\right| \le 2\sum_{k>d}|J_k(\tau)| \le \frac{2(|\tau|/2)^{d+1}}{(d+1)!\left(1-|\tau|/(2(d+2))\right)}$$
whenever $|\tau|/(2(d+2))<1$. In the OP4 simulator, $\rho=\epsilon^2/10000$ and the factorial-tail stopping test therefore certifies truncation error at most $\rho/8$; rounding each coefficient to error at most $\rho/(32(d+1))$ keeps the combined polynomial error below $\rho$. For the nontrivial simulation regime $|\tau|>\epsilon$, an integer $d$ passing OP4's test exists with
$$d=O\left(|\tau|+\frac{\ln(1/\epsilon)}{\ln(e+\ln(1/\epsilon)/|\tau|)}\right).$$
For $|\tau|\le\epsilon$, the constant polynomial $1$ approximates the target within $\epsilon$; the wrapper algorithm uses the exact identity circuit in that branch.

Let $p\in\mathbb R[x]$ be supplied exactly, with degree bound $d\ge0$, parity $d\bmod2$, $|p(x)|\le1$ on $[-1,1]$, and rational tolerance $\delta>0$. On a `SUCCESS` output of [[alg-qa-23-qsp-phase-synthesis]], the exact phase list has an ideal QSP matrix whose upper-left matrix entry $P$ satisfies $\operatorname{Re}P=p$ in exact mode and $|\operatorname{Re}P(x)-p(x)|\le\delta_0/8\le\delta/8$ in numerical mode, for every $x\in[-1,1]$, where $\delta_0=\min(\delta,8)$. If numerical phase gates are used, each compiled phase error is at most $\delta_0/(8(d+1))$ in operator norm, so the implemented upper-left matrix entry has real-part error at most $\delta_0/4\le\delta$. This is a matrix-entry accuracy claim; no measurement or scalar-extraction circuit is included. The algorithm terminates on every promised input when its optional compiler terminates with a certificate or an explicit failure result; failed exact checks return their declared non-success branch.

In `efficient-numerical` mode without a supplied complement or finite-basis compiler, the algorithm requires $\operatorname{poly}(d,1+\log_+(1/\delta))$ charged arithmetic operations, ideal exact algebraic field/equality/order tests, root-descriptor operations, and polynomially many written tower/DAG certificate bits. Here $\log_+(x)=\max(0,\log x)$. Input reading and conversion from an arbitrary original coefficient encoding, expanded minimal-polynomial conversion, operation implementation bit cost, and optional compiler work are separate resource coordinates. This is the explicit exact-algebraic arithmetic model of the algorithm; complete modes retain finite termination without the same height-independent bound.

Let $A:H_R\to H_L$ be the PUE map of [[def-qa-24-pue-svd-data]], with positive singular pairs $(\sigma_j,v_j,u_j)$, and let $\Phi=(\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_d)$ be the exact phase list in [[alg-qa-24-qsvt]]. Let $P_\Phi$ be the upper-left scalar polynomial of its QSP signal sequence. On every positive two-dimensional singular plane from [[lem-qa-24-pue-svd-invariant-subspaces]], the QSVT sequence is exactly $U_\Phi(\sigma_j)$. Consequently, if $d$ is odd,

$$\Pi_LU_\Phi\Pi_R\big|_{H_R}=\sum_{j=1}^{r}P_\Phi(\sigma_j)|u_j\rangle\langle v_j|=\bigl(P_\Phi\bigr)^{\mathrm{SV}}_{\mathrm{odd}}(A),$$

and if $d$ is even,

$$\Pi_RU_\Phi\Pi_R\big|_{H_R}=\sum_{j=1}^{r}P_\Phi(\sigma_j)|v_j\rangle\langle v_j|+P_\Phi(0)\Pi_{\ker A}=\bigl(P_\Phi\bigr)^{\mathrm{SV}}_R(A).$$

The formulas include singular values $0$ and $1$, repeated singular values, unmatched left and right kernels, and zero-dimensional singular spaces. If $p\in\mathbb R[x]$ has parity $d\bmod2$ and $|p(x)|\le1$ on $[-1,1]$, the exact completion and phase-factorization suppliers give a phase list with $\operatorname{Re}P_\Phi=p$. The coherent $\Phi$/$-\Phi$ branch then has compressed block $p^{\mathrm{SV}}(A)$; for a supplied uniform scalar error $\eta$, its block differs from $p^{\mathrm{SV}}(A)$ by at most $\eta$.

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space and let $\Pi$ be an orthogonal projection. The operators $R_\Pi=2\Pi-I$ and $S_\Pi=I-2\Pi$ are self-adjoint unitary involutions, with $R_\Pi=-S_\Pi$. On $\operatorname{ran}\Pi$ they act as $+I$ and $-I$, respectively; on $\ker\Pi$ they act as $-I$ and $+I$. In control-first order,

$$C(S_\Pi)=(Z_C)C(R_\Pi),\qquad Z_C:=\operatorname{diag}(I_H,-I_H)=Z\otimes I_H.$$

For compatible linear maps between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces,

$$\lVert ST\rVert\le \lVert S\rVert\,\lVert T\rVert.$$

For every such linear map $T$,

$$\lVert T^*T\rVert=\lVert T\rVert^2.$$

Let $V,W:H\to K\otimes E$ be linear isometries between finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, meaning $V^*V=W^*W=I_H$, and assume $\delta\ge0$ and $\|V-W\|_{\rm op}\le\delta$. For every nonzero finite-dimensional reference space $R$ and density matrix $\rho$ on $H\otimes R$ (a positive semidefinite matrix of trace one), define $V_R=V\otimes I_R$ and $W_R=W\otimes I_R$ on the ordered product bases. Define the partial trace by
$$(\operatorname{Tr}_E X)_{(k,r),(k',r')}=\sum_e X_{(k,e,r),(k',e,r')},$$
and define $\|X\|_1$ as the sum of singular values and $D(\sigma,\omega)=\tfrac12\|\sigma-\omega\|_1$. The output density matrices
$$\rho_V=(\operatorname{Tr}_E\otimes I_R)(V_R\rho V_R^*),\qquad \rho_W=(\operatorname{Tr}_E\otimes I_R)(W_R\rho W_R^*)$$
satisfy $D(\rho_V,\rho_W)\le\delta$. Tensor products use the ordered product orthonormal basis and product inner product; the displayed matrix formula fixes the partial-trace convention used here. For column vectors, $a^*$ denotes conjugate transpose and $aa^*$ the rank-one matrix with entries $a_i\overline{a_j}$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let $K=K^*$ on $H$, and let $\alpha>0$ satisfy $\|K\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\alpha$. Put $A=K/\alpha$. Let $U$ be a unitary on an ancilla-system space $H_A\otimes H$, let $J:H\to H_A\otimes H$ be the isometry $Jv=|0^a\rangle\otimes v$, and let $\Pi=JJ^*$. An **exact Hermitian block encoding** is the data $(U,J,\alpha)$ with $J^*UJ=A$. The matrix $K$ is Hermitian; $U$ itself need not be Hermitian.

The signal-register reflection is $R_\Pi=2\Pi-I$. The access record lists, separately, each supplied call to $U$, $U^*$, controlled-$U$, controlled-$U^*$, and $R_\Pi$, together with their circuit, query, gate, width, ancilla, precision, and classical-generation costs from [[def-qa-22-block-encoding-access-model]] and [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]. A state description or block matrix alone supplies none of these calls. A controlled reflection is also separate. Any PREPARE, SELECT, sparse-location, value, or coefficient operation used by a construction is a separately supplied, reversible interface with its inverse and cost recorded.

Here is the standard-form **qubiterate** for this access instance. Add a flag qubit and define $\widetilde U=|0\rangle\langle0|\otimes U+|1\rangle\langle1|\otimes U^*$, $J'v=|+\rangle\otimes Jv$, $S=X\otimes I$, $F=S\widetilde U$, and $W_{\mathrm q}=(2J'J'^*-I)F$. Implementing $\widetilde U$ requires the separately declared controlled-$U$ and controlled-$U^*$ calls; $S$, the preparation of $|+\rangle$, and the reflection about $\operatorname{ran}(J')$ also have declared costs. [[thm-qa-25-qubitization-signal-sequence]] proves its compressed block and spectral relation.

For the QSVT simulation sequence, the signal operations are the alternating $U,U^*$ calls interleaved with the projector phases $e^{i\phi(2\Pi-I)}$ from [[def-qa-23-qsp-signal-sequence]]. Their exact phase list, parity, real-polynomial extraction, controls, inverse calls, and phase-synthesis precision are part of the supplied circuit description. The scalar polynomial pairs must satisfy [[def-qa-23-qsp-admissible-polynomial-pair]]; singular-value transformations use the convention of [[def-qa-24-singular-value-transform]].

derivations.claim: If $t=0$, [F1] returns the identity circuit with no signal query, and $e^{-itH}=I$; hence its clean-input isometry error is zero. If $t\ne0$, continue with the certified OP4 output.

On an eigenvector of $H$ with eigenvalue $\lambda$, $H/\alpha$ has eigenvalue $x=\lambda/\alpha\in[-1,1]$, by [F8] and [F9]. Put $Q=E-iO$ and $B=1+2\rho$. The OP4 certificate gives $\|Q-f_\tau\|_{[-1,1]}\le\rho$ by [F1]–[F2], and $|f_\tau(x)|=1$. Since $M=Q/B$, $|M(x)-f_\tau(x)|\le |Q(x)-f_\tau(x)|/B +(B-1)|f_\tau(x)|/B \le 3\rho/(1+2\rho)<3\rho.$ The finite spectral calculus therefore gives $\|M(H/\alpha)-e^{-itH}\|_{\rm op}<\eta:=3\rho$. The two real QSVT extractions act on each eigenspace by their scalar polynomials by [F3]–[F4], so their coefficient-qubit combination has clean block $M/2$.

Let $P$ be the clean-work projector and $B=PWP=M/2$ the compressed block of the complete even/odd circuit $W$, by step 1.2. Expanding $R=I-2P$ gives $P(-WRW^*RW)P=3B-4BB^*B=3M/2-MM^*M/2.$ Indeed, $RWP=WP-2B$, $W^*RWP=P-2W^*B$, and a second application of $R$, followed by $PW$, yields $-3B+4B(PW^*P)B=-3B+4BB^*B$ before the leading minus sign. The full OAA circuit $C=-WRW^*RW$ is unitary by [F5].

Since $\|M\|_{\rm op}\le1+\eta$, telescoping $MM^*M-VV^*V$ into three factors gives $\|MM^*M-V\|_{\rm op}\le\eta\bigl((1+\eta)^2+(1+\eta)+1\bigr).$ By step 2.1, $D=3M/2-MM^*M/2$, so $\|D-V\|_{\rm op}\le\tfrac32\eta+\tfrac12\eta\bigl((1+\eta)^2+(1+\eta)+1\bigr)\le4\eta,$ where the last inequality follows from $\eta\le3/10000<1/100$. Here $D=P C P|_{\operatorname{ran}P}$ is the clean block.

Write $CJ_{\rm clean}=J_{\rm clean}D+L$, where $L=(I-P)CJ_{\rm clean}$ is the work-space leakage. Unitarity of $C$ gives $L^*L=I-D^*D$, and $D$ is a contraction as a compression of $C$. Thus $\|L\|_{\rm op}^2=\|I-D^*D\|_{\rm op} \le\|D^*(D-V)\|_{\rm op}+\|(D^*-V^*)V\|_{\rm op} \le 2\|D-V\|_{\rm op}\le8\eta.$ It follows that $\|CJ_{\rm clean}-J_{\rm clean}V\|_{\rm op}\le4\eta+\sqrt{8\eta}\le10\sqrt{\eta}$, since $\eta<1$ implies $4\eta\le4\sqrt\eta$ and $\sqrt8<3$.

Because $\eta=3\epsilon^2/10000$, $10\sqrt{\eta}=(\sqrt3/10)\epsilon$. Adding the post-amplification implementation budget $\epsilon/4$ from [F1] gives at most $(\sqrt3/10+1/4)\epsilon<\epsilon$. This is the asserted clean-input isometry error, with the residual leakage retained in $V_{\rm impl}J_{\rm clean}$.

The $t=0$ branch has zero isometry error by step 1.1; when $t\ne0$, step 5.1 gives error at most $\epsilon$. Apply [F7] in either case; it includes arbitrary reference systems and discarding the work registers, so the trace distance is at most $\epsilon$.

**Input.** An exact Hermitian block encoding of $H/\alpha$, $\alpha>0$, a rational time $t$, $0<\epsilon<1$, and a terminating certified comparison of $\tau=\alpha|t|$ with $\epsilon$, charged under the access model.

**Instructions.**

1. If $\tau\le\epsilon$, return the identity circuit on the system, with every work register left at zero. The query, gate, and bit costs of this branch are zero.
2. If $\tau>\epsilon$, invoke [[alg-qa-25-qubitized-hamiltonian-simulation]] with $t,\epsilon$, and return its circuit and error certificate. Propagate any INVALID, CERTIFICATE_ERROR, or IMPLEMENTATION_ERROR result without labeling it a successful simulation.

The comparison cost is recorded separately. The second branch is exactly the OP4 procedure; this wrapper does not modify OP4 or infer inverse, controlled, state-preparation, or phase-synthesis access.

For the exact access model of [[def-qa-25-qubitization-access-model]], rational $t$, and $0<\epsilon\le1$, a successful execution of [[alg-qa-25-qubitized-hamiltonian-simulation]] returns a unitary dilation $V_{\rm impl}$ satisfying
$$\|V_{\rm impl}J_{\rm clean}-J_{\rm out}e^{-itH}\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon$$
on the clean-input isometry $J_{\rm clean}$, where $J_{\rm out}$ appends every work register in zero. Output work registers are approximate; no full-space error on arbitrary dirty work inputs or exact cleanup is asserted. For $t=0$, the declared identity branch is exact. For every reference system, tracing out work gives the corresponding system-output trace-distance bound at most $\epsilon$.

In this page a **Hamiltonian** is a self-adjoint endomorphism $H$ of a
finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $V$; no physical postulate is
part of the term. Let $\sigma(H)$ be the set of its distinct eigenvalues and
let $P_\lambda$ be the orthogonal projection onto the $\lambda$-eigenspace.
For real time $t$, define the finite matrix evolution

$$U_H(t):=\sum_{\lambda\in\sigma(H)}e^{-it\lambda}P_\lambda = f_t(H),\qquad f_t(\lambda)=e^{-it\lambda}.$$

The second expression uses the finite spectral functional calculus
[[def-functional-calculus-for-a-normal-endomorphism]]. If $V$ is the zero
space, the spectrum is empty and the empty sum is the unique endomorphism,
which is also the identity on $V$. This definition specifies a mathematical
unitary from a finite matrix; it makes no claim that the operation has an
efficient circuit or a free access cost.

Let $H$ be a self-adjoint endomorphism of a finite-dimensional complex
inner-product space $V$. For real $t,s$, the evolution from
[[def-qa-19-finite-matrix-dynamics]] satisfies
$$U_H(0)=I_V,\qquad U_H(t)^*U_H(t)=I_V,\qquad U_H(t+s)=U_H(t)U_H(s),\qquad \frac{d}{dt}U_H(t)=-iHU_H(t).$$
Moreover, $U_H$ is the unique differentiable map $Y:\mathbb R\to
\operatorname{End}(V)$ satisfying $Y'(t)=-iHY(t)$ and $Y(0)=I_V$.

For compatible linear maps between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces,

$$\lVert ST\rVert\le \lVert S\rVert\,\lVert T\rVert.$$

For every such linear map $T$,

$$\lVert T^*T\rVert=\lVert T\rVert^2.$$

Let $V,W:H\to K\otimes E$ be linear isometries between finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, meaning $V^*V=W^*W=I_H$, and assume $\delta\ge0$ and $\|V-W\|_{\rm op}\le\delta$. For every nonzero finite-dimensional reference space $R$ and density matrix $\rho$ on $H\otimes R$ (a positive semidefinite matrix of trace one), define $V_R=V\otimes I_R$ and $W_R=W\otimes I_R$ on the ordered product bases. Define the partial trace by
$$(\operatorname{Tr}_E X)_{(k,r),(k',r')}=\sum_e X_{(k,e,r),(k',e,r')},$$
and define $\|X\|_1$ as the sum of singular values and $D(\sigma,\omega)=\tfrac12\|\sigma-\omega\|_1$. The output density matrices
$$\rho_V=(\operatorname{Tr}_E\otimes I_R)(V_R\rho V_R^*),\qquad \rho_W=(\operatorname{Tr}_E\otimes I_R)(W_R\rho W_R^*)$$
satisfy $D(\rho_V,\rho_W)\le\delta$. Tensor products use the ordered product orthonormal basis and product inner product; the displayed matrix formula fixes the partial-trace convention used here. For column vectors, $a^*$ denotes conjugate transpose and $aa^*$ the rank-one matrix with entries $a_i\overline{a_j}$.

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let $K=K^*$ on $H$, and let $\alpha>0$ satisfy $\|K\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\alpha$. Put $A=K/\alpha$. Let $U$ be a unitary on an ancilla-system space $H_A\otimes H$, let $J:H\to H_A\otimes H$ be the isometry $Jv=|0^a\rangle\otimes v$, and let $\Pi=JJ^*$. **Input.** An exact Hermitian block encoding of $H/\alpha$, $\alpha>0$, a rational time $t$, $0<\epsilon<1$, and a terminating certified comparison of $\tau=\alpha|t|$ with $\epsilon$, charged under the access model.

**Instructions.**

1. If $\tau\le\epsilon$, return the identity circuit on the system, with every work register left at zero. The query, gate, and bit costs of this branch are zero.
2. If $\tau>\epsilon$, invoke [[alg-qa-25-qubitized-hamiltonian-simulation]] with $t,\epsilon$, and return its circuit and error certificate. Propagate any INVALID, CERTIFICATE_ERROR, or IMPLEMENTATION_ERROR result without labeling it a successful simulation.

The comparison cost is recorded separately. The second branch is exactly the OP4 procedure; this wrapper does not modify OP4 or infer inverse, controlled, state-preparation, or phase-synthesis access.

With $J_k,T_k$ defined in [[def-qa-25-hamiltonian-simulation-polynomial]], for every real $\tau$ and integer $d\ge0$,
$$\sup_{|x|\le1}\left|\exp(-i\tau x)-\left(J_0(\tau)+2\sum_{k=1}^{d}(-i)^kJ_k(\tau)T_k(x)\right)\right| \le 2\sum_{k>d}|J_k(\tau)| \le \frac{2(|\tau|/2)^{d+1}}{(d+1)!\left(1-|\tau|/(2(d+2))\right)}$$
whenever $|\tau|/(2(d+2))<1$. In the OP4 simulator, $\rho=\epsilon^2/10000$ and the factorial-tail stopping test therefore certifies truncation error at most $\rho/8$; rounding each coefficient to error at most $\rho/(32(d+1))$ keeps the combined polynomial error below $\rho$. For the nontrivial simulation regime $|\tau|>\epsilon$, an integer $d$ passing OP4's test exists with
$$d=O\left(|\tau|+\frac{\ln(1/\epsilon)}{\ln(e+\ln(1/\epsilon)/|\tau|)}\right).$$
For $|\tau|\le\epsilon$, the constant polynomial $1$ approximates the target within $\epsilon$; the wrapper algorithm uses the exact identity circuit in that branch.

For degree $d\ge0$, one un-controlled QSVT sequence makes exactly $d$ signal calls: $\lceil d/2\rceil$ calls to $U$ and $\lfloor d/2\rfloor$ calls to $U^*$, beginning with $U$ when $d>0$. It applies exactly $d+1$ projector-phase operations, with $\lceil(d+1)/2\rceil$ about $\Pi_R$ and $\lfloor(d+1)/2\rfloor$ about $\Pi_L$. By [[thm-qa-24-projector-phase-implementation]], each phase operation uses two controlled calls to the corresponding reflection and one variable one-qubit phase rotation, plus a constant number of one-qubit gates. A coherent control of one sequence against the identity requires no controlled signal call when $d$ is even and one controlled signal call when $d$ is odd. Selecting between the two phase lists $\Phi$ and $-\Phi$ uses the same unconditioned signal list in both branches and controls only the phase rotations. Phase generation, inverse access, and finite-gate compilation retain their separately declared costs. At $d=0$ there is no signal or controlled-signal call.

A length-$d$ sequence from [[def-qa-23-qsp-signal-sequence]] has exactly $d$ signal factors $W_R(x)$ and exactly $d+1$ phase factors $Z(\phi_j)$, for $0\le j\le d$. In the scalar QSP model the signal acts on one two-dimensional signal register. If each $W_R$ is provided by a named query oracle, the sequence uses exactly $d$ calls to that oracle; it makes no controlled or inverse signal calls. The oracle's work registers, implementation, and query/gate charges are those explicitly supplied with it. The phase-rotation, ordinary-gate, circuit-description, bit, and numerical-precision coordinates remain separate as in [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]].

Let $A$ be a finite square or rectangular matrix with a declared isometric padding $\widehat A$, and let $\alpha>0$ satisfy $\alpha\ge\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}$. Let $B$ be the exact compressed PUE block of the supplied input unitary and assume

$$\|B-\widehat A/\alpha\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{BE}}.$$

Let $P$ be the degree-$d$ parity polynomial of an admissible QSVT phase sequence, and let $f$ have the same parity. Put $S:=\{0\}\cup\{\sigma_j:\sigma_j>0\text{ is a singular value of }\widehat A/\alpha\}$, so zero is included even when the two matrix dimensions differ. If $\sup_{\sigma\in S}|P(\sigma)-f(\sigma)|\le\eta_{\mathrm{poly}}$, and the implemented phase operation at slot $\ell$ is a unitary within operator-norm error $\zeta_\ell$ of its ideal operation, then the implemented compressed block $\widetilde B$ satisfies

$$\|\widetilde B-f^{\mathrm{SV}}(\widehat A/\alpha)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\eta_{\mathrm{poly}}+4d\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{BE}}}+\sum_{\ell}\zeta_\ell.$$

The exact sequence uses $d$ calls alternating between $U$ and $U^*$, $d+1$ projector-phase operations, and the reflection and one-qubit resources in [[thm-qa-24-qsvt-query-count]]. A real-polynomial control wrapper has its separately listed controlled gates. Matrix-data access, block-encoding construction, inverse and controlled access, phase-list generation, finite-gate compilation, and classical bit costs are charged through their declared interfaces; no cost follows from a bare matrix.

For a nonzero $d_H$-row-sparse Hermitian $H$, the designated all-zero auxiliary compression of $U_L^*U_R$ from [[alg-qa-25-sparse-hamiltonian-block-encoding]] is $H/(d_Hh_{\max})$. No constant-cost conversion from XOR locations to in-place permutations is asserted.

For the exact access model of [[def-qa-25-qubitization-access-model]], rational $t$, and $0<\epsilon\le1$, a successful execution of [[alg-qa-25-qubitized-hamiltonian-simulation]] returns a unitary dilation $V_{\rm impl}$ satisfying

When $0<c\le\tau\le C<\infty$ and $\epsilon\to0$, $L=\ln(1/\epsilon)\to\infty$ and $\ln(e+L/\tau)=\Theta(\ln L)$, since $L/C\le L/\tau\le L/c$. Substituting this comparison into $S$ gives $O(\tau+L/\ln L)$, the stated standard-regime form. Correctness remains the separate theorem [F7].

Let $(U,J,\alpha)$ be an exact Hermitian block encoding from [[def-qa-25-qubitization-access-model]], and choose an orthonormal eigenbasis $K\psi_j=\lambda_j\psi_j$. Put $x_j=\lambda_j/\alpha$ and $s_j=\sqrt{1-x_j^2}$. For $|x_j|<1$, define
$$\eta_j=(I-\Pi)UJ\psi_j/s_j,\qquad \widetilde\eta_j=(I-\Pi)U^*J\psi_j/s_j.$$
The $\eta_j$ are orthonormal in $\ker\Pi$, as are the $\widetilde\eta_j$. In the paired input basis $(J\psi_j,\widetilde\eta_j)$ and output basis $(J\psi_j,\eta_j)$, $U$ has matrix
$$\begin{pmatrix}x_j&s_j\\s_j&-x_j\end{pmatrix}.$$
The unitary $U^*$ maps in the reverse direction by the same matrix. If $|x_j|=1$, the complement is absent and $UJ\psi_j=x_jJ\psi_j=U^*J\psi_j$; no division by zero is used. The value $x_j=0$ is an ordinary two-dimensional signal plane.

derivations.claim: Since $s^2=1-x^2$, direct multiplication gives $U_x^*=U_x$ and $U_x^2=I$. Also $J^*U_xJ=[x]=K/\alpha$, so $U_x$ is unitary and has the claimed block encoding. Its clean and complementary components are $U_x|0\rangle=x|0\rangle+s|1\rangle$.

If $|x|<1$, then $s>0$, so the normalized complement defined in [F1] is $|1\rangle$; both input and output paired bases are $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$, and the matrix is exactly $U_x$. At $x=0$, $s=1$, hence $U_0=X$, confirming that zero is a regular two-dimensional signal plane.

If $x=1$ or $x=-1$, then $s=0$ and $U_x|0\rangle=x|0\rangle=U_x^*|0\rangle$. No complement vector is normalized in these cases; this verifies the endpoint convention and the encoded eigenvalue $\lambda/\alpha=x$.

Let $\mathcal B_n$ be the complex inner-product space with orthonormal basis $\{|y\rangle:y\in\{0,1\}^n\}$. For $0\le i\le n$, let $|D_i^n\rangle$ be the normalized uniform sum of basis vectors of Hamming weight $i$; define $\mathcal S_n=\operatorname{span}\{|D_i^n\rangle:0\le i\le n\}$. On a separate path space with orthonormal basis $\{|i\rangle:0\le i\le n\}$, define $H_0$ to have off-diagonal entries $w_i=\sqrt{i(n+1-i)}/n$ between $|i-1\rangle$ and $|i\rangle$ for every 1≤i≤n, and all other matrix entries zero.

$$H_x=\sum_{i=1}^n w_i\sum_{b=0}^1\left(|i-1,b\rangle\langle i,b\oplus x_i|+|i,b\oplus x_i\rangle\langle i-1,b|\right).$$

The counting identity proved below gives $H_0=(2/n)J|_{\mathcal S_n}$, under the isometry $|i\rangle\mapsto|D_i^n\rangle$. Consequently $\|H_x\|_{\rm op}\le1$ and
$$e^{-iH_x\pi n/2}|0,0\rangle=(-i)^n|n,\operatorname{parity}(x)\rangle.$$

For $n\ge1$, let $H_x$ be the $2(n+1)$-dimensional, at-most-two-sparse Hermitian path matrix of [[lem-qa-25-parity-path-transfer]] for $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, with weights $w_i=\sqrt{i(n+1-i)}/n$. Put $\eta=1/(6\pi n)$, choose $b=\lceil\log_2(3\pi n)\rceil$, and round each nonzero weight to the nearest dyadic $q_i=2^{-b}\operatorname{round}(2^bw_i)$, with ties rounded upward. Let $\widetilde H_x$ be the same path matrix with weights $q_i$, and encode its entries exactly in the row-location/value XOR-oracle model of [[def-qa-20-sparse-hamiltonian-oracle-model]], using $O(\log(n+1))$ value bits for the finite set $\{0,q_1,\ldots,q_n\}$. Then $\|H_x-\widetilde H_x\|_{\rm op}\le2\eta$ and the sparse normalization $\alpha_{\rm sp}=2\max_i q_i$ lies between positive absolute constants.

Suppose a uniform sparse-oracle query algorithm uses $q$ total row-location and value-oracle calls and returns a clean-input isometry $V_xJ_{\rm clean}$ satisfying

derivations.claim: Substituting $n=2$ gives $w_1=w_2=\sqrt2/2$. For $b\in\{0,1\}$, edge 1 joins $|0,b\rangle$ to $|1,b\oplus x_1\rangle$, and edge 2 joins $|1,b\rangle$ to $|2,b\oplus x_2\rangle$. The prefix-parity basis permutation of [F1] restores the endpoint bit $x_1\oplus x_2$; equivalently, [F1] gives $(-i)^2=-1$ times the same endpoint.
